mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 2% annualized over the previous month signals inflationary pressure, leading to tighter monetary policy expectations and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of the instances where CPIAUCSL annualized increase exceeds 2%.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.3 percentage points over the previous three months signals a tightening labor market, which is typically associated with economic expansion and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are negative in > 60% of the instances where UNRATE decreases by more than 0.3pp over 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) over the previous two months signals increased demand for housing, which is a leading indicator of economic growth and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are negative in > 50% of the instances where HOUST increases.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% over the previous month signals increased economic activity, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 5-day forward returns are negative in > 60% of the instances where INDPRO increases by more than 1%.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4.5% and the GDP (GDPC1) growth rate is below 2% year-over-year, it indicates a restrictive monetary policy coupled with slowing economic growth, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are positive in > 50% of the instances where FEDFUNDS > 4.5% and GDPC1 YoY growth < 2%.

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 over the previous month and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) decreases by more than 0.2 percentage points, it signals a strong labor market, which is typically associated with economic expansion and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increase > 200k and UNRATE decrease > 0.2pp in 1 month
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are negative in > 60% of the instances where PAYEMS increases by more than 200k and UNRATE decreases by more than 0.2pp.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) by more than 1% month-over-month signals a contraction in consumer spending, which is a leading indicator of economic slowdown and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of the instances where RSAFS decreases by more than 1%.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is increased by more than 25 basis points in a single month, it signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 5-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of the instances where FEDFUNDS increases by more than 25bps.
